weeks.title: Foundations: Java for DSA, Complexity, Math, Bits, Arrays
weeks.resources: KK (Java basics → complexity lectures), Striver A2Z Step 1 (basics, maths, hashing intro), LC Explore Arrays 101
keyConcepts: Java toolkit: `int[]`, `ArrayList`, `HashMap`/`HashSet`, `Arrays.sort`/`Arrays.fill`, `Collections`, `StringBuilder`, `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, `long` overflow, and how a `Comparator` lambda works
Big-O for loops, nested loops, `log n` halving, and recursion (the recursion-tree idea); space complexity; best, average, and worst case
Maths: digit extraction, GCD (Euclid), primes and the Sieve of Eratosthenes, fast exponentiation
Bits: `&`, `|`, `^`, `~`, `<<`, `>>`, `>>>`; checking, setting, and clearing a bit; `n & (n-1)`
Arrays: traversal, in-place modification, reversal, rotation, and the matrix-as-2D-array view
weeks.milestone: You can write clean Java with collections, and you can state the time/space complexity of any loop-based code.

weeks.title: Arrays II: Two Pointers, Prefix Sum, Kadane, Intervals
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 3 (arrays easy → hard), NC Two Pointers + Arrays & Hashing videos
keyConcepts: prefix sums plus a HashMap of seen prefixes
weeks.milestone: You can recognise when a problem needs two pointers, a prefix sum, or Kadane's algorithm, and you have solved your first Hard problem (with help is fine).

weeks.title: Hashing, Strings, Sliding Window
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z (strings + sliding window section), AV Sliding Window playlist, NC Sliding Window
keyConcepts: `StringBuilder` vs string concatenation (why `+` in a loop is O(n²))
the "at most K" minus "at most K-1" trick
weeks.milestone: You can write a variable sliding window template from memory and solve most string Mediums in 30 minutes.

weeks.title: Sorting + Binary Search
weeks.resources: AB (merge sort, quick sort), Striver A2Z Step 2 (sorting) + Step 4 (binary search), AV Binary Search playlist, LC Explore Binary Search
keyConcepts: bubble/selection/insertion sort (know them, never use them)
binary search invariants (`lo <= hi` vs `lo < hi`, and `mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2`)
binary search on the answer (monotonic predicate)
weeks.milestone: You can spot a monotonic predicate and apply binary search on the answer. You know merge sort's O(n log n) proof.

weeks.title: Recursion + Backtracking
weeks.resources: KK (recursion series, the best for beginners), Striver A2Z Step 6 (recursion), AV Recursion playlist
keyConcepts: base case, recursive call, and how the call stack works
deduplication by sorting first and skipping repeated values
weeks.milestone: You can write the subsets, permutations, and combination-sum templates from memory and draw their recursion trees.

weeks.title: Linked Lists
weeks.resources: KK (linked list lectures), Striver A2Z Step 7, LC Explore Linked List
keyConcepts: implementing singly and doubly linked lists
fast/slow pointers (finding the middle, Floyd's cycle detection and cycle start)
reversing a sub-list and reversing in k-groups
HashMap + doubly linked list for LRU
weeks.milestone: You can implement LRU Cache from scratch in under 30 minutes and reverse any segment of a list without bugs.

weeks.title: Stacks, Queues, Monotonic Stack, Deque
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 9, AV Stack playlist (monotonic stack), LC Explore Queue & Stack
keyConcepts: `ArrayDeque` as both stack and queue (never use `Stack`)
monotonic stack (next greater/smaller element, previous smaller element)
monotonic deque for sliding window max
weeks.milestone: When you see "next greater" or "previous smaller" in a problem, you think monotonic stack immediately.

weeks.title: Binary Trees
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 13 (the tree series is excellent), KK (trees), LC Explore Binary Tree, VisuAlgo
keyConcepts: BFS level order with a queue
height/depth computed bottom-up with return values
the "global answer + return a different value" pattern (diameter, max path sum)
converting a tree to a graph (parent map)
weeks.milestone: You can solve 80% of tree Mediums with "what does my recursive call return?" thinking.

weeks.title: BST, Heaps / Priority Queue, Tries
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Steps 14 (BST), 17 (heaps), and 16 (tries) · AV Heap playlist · `TreeMap`/`TreeSet` docs (`floorKey`, `ceilingKey`)
keyConcepts: top-K problems using a heap of size K
weeks.milestone: You can pick the right tool among `PriorityQueue`, `TreeMap`, and a trie. You can explain the O(n log k) cost of the top-K approach.

weeks.title: Graphs I: Traversal, Grids, Cycles, Topological Sort
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 15 (graph series, the best free graph course), WF (graph theory playlist), NC Graphs
keyConcepts: BFS/DFS on graphs and grids (4-direction arrays)
cycle detection in undirected graphs (parent tracking) and directed graphs (DFS colouring)
BFS shortest path on unweighted graphs
weeks.milestone: You can turn a word problem into a graph (nodes = ?, edges = ?) and choose between BFS, DFS, and topological sort.

weeks.title: Graphs II (Shortest Paths, DSU, MST, Bridges) + Greedy
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 15 (second half), AB (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Prim, Kruskal), WF (Union-Find, Tarjan), Striver A2Z Step 12 (greedy)
keyConcepts: Dijkstra with a `PriorityQueue` (and why it fails with negative edges)
Union-Find with path compression and union by rank
greedy: the exchange argument, sorting by end time, "why does greedy work here?"
weeks.milestone: You can write Dijkstra and DSU from memory in under 10 minutes each, and you can justify a greedy choice instead of guessing.

weeks.title: Dynamic Programming I
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 16 (the DP series is excellent), AV Dynamic Programming playlist (knapsack and LCS families), NC 1-D DP / 2-D DP
keyConcepts: recursion → memoisation → tabulation → space optimisation (do all four for the first 10 problems)
weeks.milestone: For any DP problem you can write the state, transition, and base case in words before you code.

weeks.title: DP II + Advanced (Segment Tree, Fenwick Tree, KMP)
weeks.resources: Striver A2Z Step 16 (second half), AV (Matrix Chain Multiplication playlist), WF (segment tree, Fenwick tree), CPA (prefix function / KMP)
keyConcepts: LIS in O(n²) and in O(n log n) with binary search
stock problems as a state machine
weeks.milestone: ~300+ problems solved across every core topic. You have a personal template file for each pattern.

phases.name: Foundation

A.name: Glute bridge
A.tip: Squeeze your glutes at the top for 1 s; keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch

A.name: Bird dog
A.tip: Move slowly, keeping your hips level as if there's a cup of tea on your back

A.name: Standing calf raise (hold a wall)
A.tip: Pause 1 s at the top and lower slowly

A.name: Dead bug
A.tip: Press your lower back into the floor the whole time

B.name: Wall sit
B.tip: Back flat on the wall; go only as low as is comfortable

B.name: Incline push-up (kitchen counter)
B.tip: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, elbows at 45°, not flared out

B.tip: Step back, then lower straight down; front knee over the middle of your foot

B.name: Hip hinge (bodyweight good-morning)
B.tip: Push your hips back like closing a car door with your butt; flat back

B.name: Incline plank (hands on a table)
B.tip: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs as if bracing for a poke

B.name: Prone Y-raise (lying face down)
